correctness.rationale: The conditional log-cosh identity holds algebraically for every positive kernel and uniform target margins. Strict positivity makes the log-partition coercive and strictly convex, so strict coordinate potential decrease for |1-omega|<1 implies global convergence by compactness and uniqueness. At omega=2 both half-steps preserve the potential exactly; at omega>2 it increases away from conditional minimizers, proving the universal sharp boundary. The affine scalar recurrence has factor (1-omega)^2<1, upgrading ratio convergence to unnormalized coupling convergence. The 2x2 Jacobian Schur inequalities are strictly positive throughout 0<omega<2. The diagnostic rederives identities from the original multiplicative equations.

value.rationale: This resolves a genuine local-versus-global stability gap for a recognized fixed overrelaxed optimal-transport scaling method. The published general guarantee omega<2/(1+Lambda(K)) can become arbitrarily conservative as Lambda(K) tends to one, while all positive balanced 2x2 kernels remain globally stable for any fixed omega<2. A conserved log-partition at omega=2 explains the sharp loss of convergence. The result is a meaningful complete classification for the smallest interacting transport problem, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
